Subject: Pricing proposal follow-up — committed vs paygo

Soojin — thanks for the demo yesterday. Quick note from procurement: Medisuite is interested in moving from our current pay-as-you-go test to a 12-month committed package, but we need a one-time commercial concession to offset our initial onboarding/validation costs.

High level ask:
- 12-month committed token pool (~12M tokens/month)
- 30% credit applied to onboarding/validation costs (one-time) OR a one-time invoice credit (~$40k)
- 60-day procurement signoff target if commercial terms acceptable

Can you share what commercial authority you need to make this happen? Tim

Subject: Fwd: Pricing proposal follow-up — committed vs paygo (need signoff on one-time sweetener)

Marissa / Markus (Kim on copy) — forwarding the Medisuite ask. They want to move to a 12-month commit but are requesting a one-time onboarding/validation concession (~$40k or 30% of onboarding costs). Attached is the pricing model I ran through — shows unit economics with the commit and a proposed ramp credit.

Recommendation I'm proposing for internal approval so we can get to contracting quickly:
- Offer: 12-month committed pool (12M tokens/month) at standard committed rate
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% of TCV first year (capped at $45,000) — applied as pre-invoice credit on month 1
- Requirement: non-refundable 12-month minimum and 30 days to sign from final SOW

Why: This preserves acceptable unit economics while giving them the cashflow smoothing they asked for. I think a cap protects revenue downside. We need VP/CFO signoff on the sweetener authority (we're slightly outside standard playbooks).

Attachments: Medisuite_Pricing_Model_v2.xlsx, MA-Plan_Draft_2026-12.pdf

Can you review and advise signoff language? SOON is ideal — procurement wants DocuSign by end of week.

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing proposal follow-up — committed vs paygo (need signoff on one-time sweetener)

Soojin — looked through the model. Quick thoughts:
- 15% sweetener (cap $45k) as a one-time credit is reasonable for a 12-month non-refundable commit at the size they propose.
- Request we add a clear clawback: if they breach commit (drop below 70% of monthly average for two consecutive months) we reserve the right to recoup a prorated portion of the credit in the final invoice.
- Suggest invoice mechanics: apply credit month 1 as a deduction; show line item and expiration clause.

Suggested signoff note for VP/CFO: "Approved one-time onboarding credit up to 15% of TCV (cap $45k) contingent on execution of 12-month minimum commit and inclusion of a recoup clause for sustained under-delivery. Approval limited to this specific Medisuite transaction."

I support moving forward if legal ok's the clause. Recommend obtaining exec signoff from Markus (VP Sales) and Kim (CFO) to finalize.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Requesting CFO clearance: Medisuite one-time onboarding credit (candidate approval language below)

Kim — Per the thread below, Medisuite is willing to commit to a 12-month minimum pool that materially improves unit economics. Marissa recommends a one-time onboarding credit up to 15% of TCV (cap $45k) with a recoup clause if they under-deliver.

Commercial ask: please sign off the following language (or provide edits):

"CFO Approval: Approved one-time onboarding credit of up to 15% of first-year TCV (not to exceed $45,000) for Medisuite Health (Deal: DEAL-8471). Approval conditioned upon: (1) execution of a 12-month non-refundable minimum committed token pool; (2) inclusion of a recoup clause allowing Redwood to prorate and reclaim unused onboarding credit if Medisuite fails to meet 70% of the monthly commit for two consecutive months; (3) offer limited to the specific Medisuite commercial agreement and not a precedent."

This is time-sensitive — contracting wants to send DocuSign by Friday. Approve or flag changes and we'll incorporate legal language.

Thanks — Markus

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Requesting CFO clearance: Medisuite one-time onboarding credit (candidate approval language below)

Markus / team — I reviewed the ask and the attached economics. Approve with modifications:

- Approval level: ONE-TIME concession approved at up to 12% of first-year TCV, capped at $35,000 (reduced from request).
- Conditionalities: commit must be non-refundable 12 months; onboarding credit applied as month-1 invoice credit; recoup clause applies if average monthly consumption <70% of committed pool for two consecutive billing months — recoup calculated pro rata on the outstanding credit.
- Non-precedent clause required.

Please update the signoff text to reflect the 12% / $35k limit and send the final SOW to me for countersignature. If Legal needs to tweak the recoup language, loop them in, but do not delay DocuSign more than 48 hours unless material changes are requested by Medisuite.

Kim

Tim — thanks for the quick turnaround. Appreciate the interest in committing. Per internal review, Redwood can extend a one-time onboarding credit under the following commercial terms: 

Offer summary:
- 12-month committed token pool: 12M tokens/month
- Onboarding credit: 12% of first-year TCV, capped at $35,000 — applied as a credit on month-1 invoice
- Conditions: 12-month non-refundable minimum; recoup clause (if average consumption <70% of committed pool for two consecutive months, Redwood may prorate and reclaim unused portion of the onboarding credit)
- This concession is one-time and not a general precedent

I've attached the updated MA-Plan draft and the pricing model for transparency. If this works, please confirm and we'll route the SOW to DocuSign (link below) for signature; contracting has priority to close this week to meet your 60-day target.
